deep.reconstruction:
This page is a working draft for Riemann's 1860 memoir 'Ueber die Fortpflanzung ebener Luftwellen von endlicher Schwingungsweite' (Abh. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 8, 1860). It mixes three kinds of material.

(A) Draft of the introduction. The text says the usual linearized treatment suffices to explain the phenomena observed so far. It adds that, given the progress Helmholtz has recently made in experimental acoustics, the results of the more exact (nonlinear) calculation might soon give the experimenters some points of reference. Then comes the title.

(B) Sound-speed references, continuing the previous page's computation of k = c/c' ≈ 1.4101 against the Bravais–Martins value. The three measurements are:
- Moll & van Beek, 332.25 m/s, between two hills on the Utrecht heath (Phil. Trans. 1824, p. 424; Poggendorff's Annalen 5).
- (Stampfer) & v. Myrbach, 332.96 m/s, near Salzburg (Jahrbücher des polytechn. Instituts Wien, Bd. 7).
- Bravais & Martins, 332.37 m/s, Faulhorn.

(C) Mathematics. Notation: pressure p = φ(ρ), sound speed c = √φ'(ρ), and f(ρ) = ∫ √φ'(ρ) dρ/ρ. The Riemann invariants are
 4) f(ρ)+u = 2r, f(ρ)−u = 2s,
so that r is constant along dx/dt = u + √φ' and s along dx/dt = u − √φ'.

Hodograph step: take x and t as functions of (r,s). Then
 1) (x−(u+√φ')t) dr − (x−(u−√φ')t) ds = dw is an exact differential, hence
 2) x−(u+√φ')t = ∂w/∂r,
 3) x−(u−√φ')t = −∂w/∂s.
This is the step that makes the problem linear for w(r,s), as in §3 of the memoir.

Polytropic law φ = Aρ^k (my filling): √φ' = √(kA) ρ^{(k−1)/2}, so f = 2√φ'/(k−1). Hence r+s = f, u = r−s and √φ' = (k−1)/2·(r+s). It follows that √φ'+u = (k+1)/2·r + (k−3)/2·s, as written. Riemann also writes ∂log√φ'/∂logρ − 1 = (k−3)/2. Marginal notes discuss the slope becoming infinite: the velocity gradient becomes 'positiv unendlich', or else the density becomes infinitely small. This is the breakdown of the continuous solution and the onset of a jump.

Discontinuities (Verdichtungsstoss). Riemann uses conservation of mass and momentum with p = φ(ρ). Across a jump between states 1 and 2:
 u1−u2 = √[(ρ1−ρ2)(φ(ρ1)−φ(ρ2))/(ρ1ρ2)].
With 2r = f+u this gives
 2(r1−r2) = (u1−u2) + f(ρ1)−f(ρ2) = f(ρ1)−f(ρ2) + √[(ρ1−ρ2)(φ1−φ2)/(ρ1ρ2)].
One variant uses an intermediate state ρ' with s'+r1 = f(ρ'), i.e. r is unchanged across one wave.

Writing (ρ1−ρ2)/√(ρ1ρ2) = √(ρ1/ρ2) − √(ρ2/ρ1), the jump becomes (√(ρ1/ρ2)−√(ρ2/ρ1))·√[(φ1−φ2)/(ρ1−ρ2)]. Riemann claims this increases steadily with ρ1, because (φ1−φ2)/(ρ1−ρ2) = ∫_0^1 φ'(ρ2+α(ρ1−ρ2)) dα is the mean of φ' between ρ2 and ρ1. The substitution ρ2 = αρ1 gives the radicand (α−1)/(αρ1)·(φ(αρ1)−φ(ρ1)), as in the fragment.

Riemann problem. An initial discontinuity between states 1 and 2 can split into two shocks running in opposite directions, with an intermediate density ρ':
 u1−u2 = √[(ρ'−ρ1)(φ(ρ')−φ(ρ1))/(ρ'ρ1)] + √[(ρ'−ρ2)(φ(ρ')−φ(ρ2))/(ρ'ρ2)].
The case split rests on comparing (u1−u2)² with (ρ1−ρ2)(φ1−φ2)/(ρ1ρ2) (one shock) and with (f(ρ1)−f(ρ2))² (one simple wave). The general inequality (f1−f2)² ≤ (ρ1−ρ2)(φ1−φ2)/(ρ1ρ2) follows from Cauchy–Schwarz (my justification).

Isothermal or normalized case φ = a²ρ: f = a logρ, so u1−u2 = a(√(ρ1/ρ2)−√(ρ2/ρ1)) and 2(r1−r2) = log(ρ1/ρ2) + (√(ρ1/ρ2)−√(ρ2/ρ1))·a, as written (only consistent if a = 1). For two shocks with a = 1:
 u1−u2 = √(ρ'/ρ1)−√(ρ1/ρ') + √(ρ'/ρ2)−√(ρ2/ρ') = (√(ρ'/(ρ1ρ2)) − 1/√ρ')(√ρ1+√ρ2).
The last factor is only begun on the page ('√').
errors: The isothermal line 2(r1−r2) = log(ρ1/ρ2) + (√(ρ1/ρ2)−√(ρ2/ρ1))a is dimensionally inconsistent unless a = 1: with φ = a²ρ one has f = a logρ, so the log term should also carry a factor a. It is apparently a normalization slip.
The monotonicity claim for (√(ρ1/ρ2)−√(ρ2/ρ1))·√(mean φ') needs the mean of φ' to be non-decreasing in ρ1. That holds if φ' is increasing (φ convex, e.g. k ≥ 1 polytropic) but is not stated.
The final factorization of the two-shock velocity difference is left incomplete; the missing factor is (√ρ1+√ρ2).

As in the published memoir, the jump conditions use p = φ(ρ) (mass and momentum only, isentropic), not energy conservation. This is Riemann's well-known physical error, later corrected by Rankine and Hugoniot. It is a modelling issue, not an algebraic slip on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: This is draft material for the published 1860 memoir: the introduction mentioning Helmholtz, Riemann invariants, the hodograph w, shock conditions and the Riemann problem all appear in print. Only minor working details are unpublished, such as the explicit isothermal two-shock algebra and the mean-value monotonicity argument.

With ρ2 = αρ1 the shock radicand equals (α−1)/(αρ1)·(φ(αρ1)−φ(ρ1)) (expected 0).

transcription_corrections: 'Kendall u. v. Myrbach' should almost certainly read 'Stampfer u. v. Myrbach'. Their 1822 Salzburg measurement is published in the Jahrbücher des polytechnischen Instituts in Wien, Bd. 7.
The Salzburg location reads like 'zwischen Mönchsberg u. Untersberg bei Salzburg' rather than '... Mönchsberg u. ... bei Salzburg'.
'Bravais [?] u. Martins' is correct (cf. the previous page, 'Martins und Bravais', Faulhorn).
In line 1 the second term is −(x−(u−√φ'(ρ))t)ds; there is no stray minus sign inside.
The last line ends with the factor (√ρ1+√ρ2), only begun as '√'. It is not a free-standing radical.
The heading 'Generalversammlung ...' is uncertain; it is a source note for the sound-speed data, not part of the derivation.
The fragment after u1 = 2r1 − f(ρ1) is (α−1)/(αρ1)·(φ(αρ1) − φ(ρ1)): the shock radicand with ρ2 = αρ1.
